title: Backstage Reaction To Claudio Castagnoli In CMLL, Josh Alexander Returns To AEW, & More - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Clark ,
10 minutes ago
Claudio Castagnoli has been pulling double duty between AEW and CMLL, and a new report suggests that the former ROH World Champion has earned plenty of respect from those within the Mexican promotion.
Castagnoli has been working under a dual contract with AEW and CMLL since March, allowing him to regularly appear for both companies. According to a report from Dave Meltzer, CMLL officials and talent have been particularly impressed by Castagnoli’s ability to handle the demanding conditions inside Arena México.
The legendary venue sits nearly 7,500 feet above sea level, making its altitude a significant challenge for wrestlers who aren’t accustomed to competing there. Meltzer explained that Castagnoli has seemingly had no trouble adjusting to the environment.
Meltzer noted that Castagnoli “would fly in there and they would do these singles matches, and he would not get tired.”
That reportedly stands out because several American wrestlers have struggled with the altitude in Arena Mexico, whereas CMLL’s regular roster has become accustomed to performing at that elevation.
Castagnoli has already enjoyed considerable success in CMLL. He captured the CMLL World Heavyweight Championship in November 2025 and held the title for 118 days before dropping it to Hechicero on March 20.

His most recent CMLL appearance came in the 2026 International Grand Prix. Castagnoli competed for the entire tournament match, which lasted nearly 74 minutes, further demonstrating his impressive stamina in one of wrestling’s most physically demanding environments.
Josh Alexander is officially back in AEW.
The September 2 episode of AEW Dynamite featured Darby Allin defending the TNT Championship against Mark Davis. Following the match, Steven Borden made his way to the ring in an attempt to stop Davis from continuing his attack.
However, Borden soon found himself in trouble when Josh Alexander blindsided him from behind, marking Alexander’s first AEW appearance since March.
Alexander had been sidelined after suffering a knee injury earlier this year, keeping him away from AEW programming for several months.
The former TNA World Champion made his return to in-ring competition in August when he appeared at Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Mayhem event. Now, Alexander has made his way back to AEW television — and immediately made his presence felt with a shocking attack.
